purpose: Single source of truth for the container images the lakehouse tile bake runs, their memory caps and the work disk a bake needs (root ADR-0112 §9, ADR-0133 §3). External images are pinned by digest; the tippecanoe image is built from infra/tiles/tippecanoe/Dockerfile, which pins its base digest and source commit.

gdal.reason: ubuntu-small carries GEOS, which -makevalid needs; alpine-small does not.
gdal.memory_reason: ogr2ogr streams the CSV row by row into the GeoJSON sequence; 4g is headroom over the Seoul pilot, not a measurement. The first national bake re-measures it (root ADR-0133 §7).

tippecanoe.reason: No official image or binary release exists, so it is built from the tagged source commit.
tippecanoe.memory_reason: The Seoul pilot (898,741 parcels) peaked at 0.96GB; the national run (about 40M) is unmeasured, and its sort and tile work spill to the -t directory. The first national bake re-measures it (root ADR-0133 §7).

maxzoom_detail_reason: Root ADR-0262. tippecanoe's --full-detail for a unit, the maxzoom tile extent being 2^detail. At the default 12 (extent 4096, about 10 cm per unit at z16 in Korea) the national 202609 bake lost 542 parcels tippecanoe's polygon cleaning collapsed, slivers up to 16 px wide at render_max_zoom 22 among them. At 14 (extent 16384) one unit is one pixel at zoom 22, and every parcel still lost in the measurement is sub-pixel there, which the maxzoom id gate allows by id. zoning bakes its maxzoom at z14, so the default 12 makes one unit 16 px at render_max_zoom 22: from 2026-11-03 every zoning bake was refused, its z14 tiles missing 642 zones that are not sub-pixel (1.3 to 12 px wide at z22). Re-baking the 11,706 zones under 32 px wide of the 2026-11-07 handoff with the pinned tippecanoe lost 689 such zones at 12, 279 at 13, 52 at 14, 1 at 15 and none at 16, where one unit is again one pixel at zoom 22; that sample archive grew 17% (2.25 to 2.64 MB), and only the z14 tiles change, --full-detail being the maxzoom detail. Root ADR-0485 makes the rule every unit's, checked by every bake: 2^detail >= 256 x 2^(render_max_zoom - tile_max_zoom), one maxzoom unit at most one pixel at render_max_zoom. complex (tiles to z16, drawn to 22) baked at the default 12 measured 2026-11-09 off its Gold boundary by up to one unit at z16 (0.12 m, 4 px at zoom 22), so it is 14 like parcels; its archive is 6 MB. admin is drawn only to its tile maxzoom 16 and keeps 12. A unit not listed keeps 12.
tile_max_zoom_reason: Root ADR-0492. The zoom a unit listed here is cut to, in place of the active release's; the release the bake promotes carries it (catalog.vector_tile_build_job.tile_max_zoom). mapbox-gl re-quantises every tile to its own 8192-unit extent, so a z16 tile drawn at render_max_zoom 22 is two pixels per unit there and its edges step by up to a pixel, however fine the archive's own detail (W41, 2026-11-09). Cut to z17 at maxzoom_detail 13 (extent 8192), the archive's unit is the renderer's unit: nothing is rounded twice, a unit is one pixel at z22, and the ground precision is what z16 at detail 14 (parcels, complex) and z14 at detail 16 (zoning) gave, about 3 cm in Korea. A unit not listed keeps its active release's maxzoom.
partition_run_budget_seconds_reason: Root ADR-0493. A partitioned unit listed here starts no partition this many seconds after the run started (job per_run_cap.deadline points here). The national parcel bake measured 2026-10-13 was GDAL 60 minutes and tippecanoe 109 minutes, past the job's 115-minute limit, so its first base never fitted one run and the job stayed off. Each partition's archive lands in the create-only cache as it completes, before any Catalog or R2 write; a run at its budget prints lakehouse-tile-bake-deferred and the job's next start (twice a day) continues, and the run that finds every partition cached joins, gates, uploads and promotes. 4,200 s + the largest partition (about 1,600 s at z17) + 120 s for the stop stays under 90% of the 6,900 s limit.
partition_by_feature_id_prefix_reason: Root ADR-0316 (zoning: root ADR-0373, by layer code). A unit listed here is baked one archive per feature-id prefix and the archives are joined with tile-join (installed beside tippecanoe from the same pinned commit). For parcels the first 2 characters of the PNU are the 시도. Each archive is kept under the bake work root as <unit>-partitions/<prefix>/<sha256 of its rows and bake inputs>.pmtiles, create-only, so an edition that leaves a 시도's rows unchanged reuses that 시도's archive instead of running GDAL and tippecanoe over it again. A unit not listed is baked whole.
units_born_from_a_lakehouse_bake_reason: Root ADR-0374. A unit listed here that Catalog does not hold yet is registered by its first bake-lakehouse-tiles run with this layer, its first static release and a complete runtime manifest in one transaction; it never has a PostGIS release. Once the unit exists its layer is read from Catalog like every other unit's, so editing this entry after the birth changes nothing. zoning (root ADR-0373): the regulation zones of silver.land_use_zone_area, feature id <layer_code>:<zone_feature_id>:<sigungu_code> (partitioned by its first 4 characters, the layer), tiles 10-14 measured from the 2026-10-31 load: by bounding box at most 196 tiles at z10, 661 at z11, 2,395 at z12, 9,067 at z13 and 34,983 at z14 (47,302 in all) over 655,266 zones; at z10 an average tile already carries about 3,400 zones, at z8 26,000, so lower zooms are not baked.
feature_min_zoom_reason: Root ADR-0375 §3. A unit listed here starts the features whose property has a listed value at that zoom; every other feature starts at default. bake-lakehouse-tiles passes it to tippecanoe as one -j feature filter on $zoom (README of the pinned commit: the special variable $zoom is the current zoom level), so it is part of the bake inputs and an index or partition archive made under other inputs is not reused. Every zoom lies inside the layer's tile zooms, so every feature still reaches the maxzoom tiles the id gate reads. zoning, measured 2026-11-04 on the densest z10 tile (x=873 y=396, 35,973 zones) by encoding real MVT at extent 4096 with simplification 1 unit, a 5 px buffer and gzip (mapbox-vector-tile and shapely, tippecanoe's documented tolerance), per family: z10 urbanFacilities (D142-D148) 497 KB, landUse 281 KB, greenbelt 30 KB, factoryLocation 10 KB, agriculturalPromotion about 0 KB (all together about 818 KB); z11, the largest of its 4 tiles: 226, 138, 17, 10 and about 0 KB (about 391 KB together); z12: landUse 62, greenbelt 8, factoryLocation 6, agriculturalPromotion 1 KB. The budget is 500 KB gzip per tile, tippecanoe's own default maximum tile size and the Mapbox Tiling Service limit: the 도시계획시설 layers from z11 keep that tile under it, every other family fits at z10.
low_zoom_generalization_reason: W42 (2026-11-09): the owner saw one zoning tile and the rest never arrived. The ring of the owner's view measured from Korea served z10 tiles of 229 KB to 1.1 MB and z11 of 491 KB to 1.7 MB (uncompressed on cache hits, root ADR-0111's x-protobuf fix), 6 to 39 s each; the densest z10 tile (x=873 y=396) carried 8,202 zones and 270,389 vertices, 473,504 bytes gzip, of which the per-zone zone_id string alone was about 71 KB. The map draws and filters the layer by layer_code only (products/gongzzang zoning-families.ts), and the parcel panel reads its zones from the by-PNU lane, not from tiles. A unit listed here therefore keeps only `properties` below its maxzoom (tippecanoe -j attribute-filter on $zoom, removed while the feature is read), merges features left with equal properties (--reorder --coalesce; coalesced polygons pass tippecanoe's polygon cleaning, which unions them so shared borders disappear) and simplifies lines and polygons at `simplification` tile units (--simplification; at detail 12 four units are half a pixel of a 512-pixel tile, a quarter of a 256-pixel one: faithful at the pixel scale, Mapbox Tiling Service and tippecanoe's README both treat up to about 10 as without visible difference). Its maxzoom tiles keep every property and the standard tolerance (--simplification-at-maximum-zoom=1, the pinned README), so the id gate and the patch path read what they read before. Computed on the densest z10 tile by decoding it, dissolving by layer_code and zone_code with shapely and simplifying 4 units (an estimate of tippecanoe, not its output): 28 features, 151,123 bytes gzip (32% of before); by layer_code alone it would be 36,076. zone_code stays so a later style can colour each 용도지역 without a new bake. Changing it rebakes every partition once (the arguments are bake inputs, root ADR-0316): a declared full rebake of zoning, about one zoning bake's time on ai-server.
tile_bytes_budget_reason: W42. The bake refuses a unit listed here when any stored (compressed) tile is larger than this many bytes, read from the new archive's directories before upload; every unit's largest tile per zoom is printed as lakehouse-tile-bake-largest-tiles. 500,000 bytes is tippecanoe's own default maximum (the bake passes --no-tile-size-limit, so tippecanoe no longer enforces it) and the Mapbox Tiling Service limit; the target is about 150 KB. Without it the 2026-11 zoning releases published z11 tiles of up to 1.7 MB uncompressed that a phone in Korea took 39 s to fetch. parcels is not listed until a bake's printed largest tiles are measured under it: its archives are not kept on the host, so its largest tile is unknown and refusing it blind could stop the parcel release.
patch_buffer_pixels_reason: Root ADR-0323 §2 and ADR-0375 §2. The pixels (of a tile's 256) a feature's box is widened by when the patch path asks which tiles it touches: tippecanoe's default buffer of 5 (the bake does not set -b) plus 1 for the rounding between a box and the rendered geometry. lakehouse_tile_patch.rs BUFFER_PIXELS is this number (a test reads it here), and land_use_zone_area_by_tile.py reads it to file each regulation zone under the z10 tiles it touches, with one pixel more so its float boxes cover the bake's f32 ones. infra/lakehouse/spark/tests/fixtures/tile_range_golden.json holds boxes and the tile ranges both languages must compute for them.

work_disk.reason: The work directory holds, at its peak, the GDAL CSV (about the handoff's size), the GeoJSON sequence (larger), tippecanoe's temporary files under -t and the archive. A bake refuses to start below max(min_free_bytes, handoff bytes x min_free_bytes_per_handoff_byte). The multiple is an estimate the first national bake re-measures. In production a national unit's work root is under production_root, on /data, never the root disk.
